items.title: Review request
meta: DCI M. Askew, Major Investigation Team
items.heading: Somebody in this file has an alibi that is not what it looks like
body: Graham Lythe, 61, was found dead on the 199 Steps in Whitby, North Yorkshire, at 06:50 on Sunday 27 October 2024. He had been struck on the head and then fell down the steps.

We have a narrow time for the attack. We have five people with motives, secrets, or both. Every one of the five has an account of where they were at that time, and every account is backed by a record, a witness or both.
I don't accept that. Read the file as it stood at 17:00 today and tell me:

list: When, exactly, was he attacked (in UTC), and how was he brought onto the steps?
Which alibis are genuine, which is false, and how do you know, record by record?
What else happened that night at Saltwick Bay, who was involved, and where was the 17:04 photograph taken from? Prove it wasn't taken in the summer.
Why did Tom Ellerby lie in his first statement?

body: Times are copied exactly as they appear on each source (phone screen, device export, record) or exactly as the witness said them. Where a source names a time zone, it's shown.

Everything you need is in this file plus information that is freely available online: maps, reference sites, published records of past days. Every real-world fact in the case has been checked. If something online seems to contradict the file, look again at exactly what that source is telling you.
When you're ready, use Make your accusation. The review panel asks about the parts of the case that matter; questions 4 and 5 above are for your own satisfaction and are covered in the solution.

items.title: Summary and persons of interest
body: At 06:52 on Sunday 27 October 2024, Thomas Ellerby rang 999 to report a man lying on the 199 Steps, the stone stairway that climbs from the foot of Church Street and Henrietta Street up to St Mary's Church on Whitby's East Cliff. Paramedics confirmed life extinct at 07:09. The man was Graham Lythe of Henrietta Street, a retired geology teacher and well-known local fossil collector.

His handset shows a text message from an unknown number at 01:16. It refers to activity at Saltwick Bay. After that he made two calls that weren't answered and left his house. A neighbour heard a shout and a fall at 01:24 by her phone. Two holiday-let guests saw a man matching his description pass them on Henrietta Street "a minute or two" before they rang their host at 01:21.

On Monday 28 October at 14:10, the landowner's agent reported that a large fossil-bearing block had been removed from the foot of the cliff at Saltwick Bay. Mr Lythe had discovered the fossil in it in September.

body: Danby & Co., solicitors, hold Mr Lythe's will dated 2019. It leaves his estate to his brother Keith, or, if Keith dies first, to Keith's widow Carol and son Ryan in equal shares. Keith died in 2021. The estate is estimated at £385,000 (the cottage plus savings).

An appointment had been booked for 10:30 on Monday 28 October to sign a new will. The unsigned draft leaves £5,000 each to Carol and Ryan, and the cottage, the residue and the fossil collection to a charitable trust. Mr Danby says that on Friday 25 October Mr Lythe told him "the family know".

items.title: Scene and post-mortem
body: The deceased lay head-downhill on the steps, about fifty steps below the top landing by the churchyard. He was wearing pyjamas under a waxed jacket, with walking boots on but unlaced. Beneath the body was a black LED torch, switched on, its battery exhausted. In his pockets were his phone, house keys and a handkerchief. His front door on Henrietta Street was pulled to but not locked.

On the bench at the top landing there was one cigarette end (filter, manufactured brand), sent for DNA. Nothing else of note was found at the top. The steps were damp. There were no usable footprints.

The cause of death was head injury. There was a single depressed injury to the left side of the back of the head, made by a heavy blunt object with a rounded edge and inflicted before the fall. Multiple injuries were consistent with falling down stone steps. Blood alcohol was low. From the pathology alone, time of death can't be narrowed beyond 23:00 Saturday to 04:00 Sunday. The weapon has not been found.

items.title: Graham's notebook
items.intro: Extracts copied from the deceased's pocket notebook.

pages.text: SALTWICK! Ichthyosaur, near-complete, in the fallen block at the cliff foot below the holiday park. Told N. Nobody else yet.
C. and R. for tea. Showed them the photos. R. asked what it's worth. Told him it's worth nothing because it's going to a museum.
N. says he has "a buyer". £160k. Said no.
Showed the agent the block. Recovery with Imogen's team booked for Sat 2 Nov.
C. came round. £15k again, the arrears. Said no, and told her about Monday. She went very quiet. Said Keith would turn in his grave. Perhaps he would.

N. in the shop again about his buyer. "Last chance, Graham." Told him for the last time. Mary Ellen out past the piers this afternoon. R. in the Jet & Anchor tonight, money again. Lost my temper, shouldn't have.

items.title: Thomas Ellerby (1)
items.name: Thomas Ellerby
items.text:
I take Bramble out first thing, just as it's getting light. We went along to the steps and she went straight up and started whining, and there he was. It's Graham from up the street. I rang 999 straight away, that's it on my phone, 06:52. I didn't touch him except to see if he was breathing.

Last night? I was in, I didn't go out. I heard a shout at some point, about half one. We all did. I was at the door with my guests from the let at the time. We thought it was lads in the churchyard, they're up there most Saturdays. I wish to God we'd gone and looked.

Me and Graham? We'd had our differences. He objected to my roof terrace on the let and it got knocked back in August. That's planning, isn't it, it's not personal.

items.title: The Doyles
items.name: Mark and Sinéad Doyle (joint account)
items.text:
We're staying in Tom's cottage on Henrietta Street, we came from Leeds on Friday. Saturday night we were at a friend's fortieth in another holiday cottage on Church Street. We left about quarter past one by Mark's phone and walked back.

The key safe wouldn't open. We tried the code about five times. Just before we gave up and rang Tom, an older man in a long coat came past us really fast with a torch, heading along toward the bottom of the steps. He didn't say anything. He wasn't drunk, he was just in a hurry. That would be a minute or two before the call. Mark rang Tom at 01:21 (call log shown to officer).

Tom came down in his dressing gown and slippers and sorted the box. We were all three of us stood on the step chatting when there was a man's shout from up the steps, and then a clattering, like a bin going down. Tom said it'll be lads in the churchyard. We went in, he went home. Tom was stood right next to us when it happened, he never moved.

items.title: Peggy Harland
items.name: Margaret "Peggy" Harland
items.text:
My back bedroom looks straight onto the steps. I've lived in this house fifty-one years.

I go to bed with the wireless on. I always drop off after the shipping forecast, it's my lullaby. I woke up to spend a penny. It was about twenty past one by my phone. I looked out of the back and there was a torch going up the steps and a dog with it. Tom Ellerby's spaniel, I'd know that daft bark anywhere. Black as your hat it was, you couldn't see a thing past the torch. I went back to bed.

Then I woke again with a man shouting, sort of "What—", and then a horrible clatter, and then nothing. I looked at my phone, 01:24. That didn't make sense to me, I'd have sworn I'd been asleep a good long while. I looked out of the back and there was a light lying still on the steps, a torch, and I thought some fool's dropped it. Nobody on the steps that I could see, nobody coming down. Then I went to the front window, and Tom was at the door of his holiday cottage with a young couple, all three of them looking up toward the steps. So I thought, well, they've seen to it. I went back to bed.

I've said to everybody since: there was a man on those steps with a torch a few minutes before Graham was killed.

items.title: Thomas Ellerby (2)
items.name: Thomas Ellerby
items.text:
All right. I did go out, and I'm sorry I said I didn't. The fireworks had set Bramble off and she wouldn't settle, so I took her up the steps into the churchyard, about quarter past one. It was pitch black. I had a crafty cigarette at the top. That'll be mine on the bench. My wife thinks I've stopped, so I'd be grateful.

I was back in by twenty-five past or so and went straight up to bed. Then my phone went. It was the Doyles about the key safe, so I went down. I'd only just got my head down, it felt like minutes. And then the shout came while I was stood with them.

When I found him in the morning, all I could think was, I was up there last night, on my own, and him and me have history. They'll say it was me. So I said I never went out. Then Peggy started telling everyone she'd seen a man on the steps right before it happened, and I knew I had to come and tell you. But I never saw Graham. I never saw anybody.

items.title: Darren Hobbs
items.name: Darren Hobbs
items.occupation: Bar manager, the Jet & Anchor, Church Street
items.text: Graham came in about six, sat at the end with his usual half. Ryan came in about seven and sat with him. They were all right at first. It went off right at the end of the Everton game, the late one on the big screen. Everton equalised in about the last minute and half the bar went up. In the middle of all that, Ryan's shouting at his uncle, "You'd rather give it to a museum than your own family." Ryan went out and slammed the door. Graham stayed till about nine and said he was off to bed early, big week coming.

items.title: Ryan Lythe
items.name: Ryan Lythe
items.text:
After the pub I went home to my flat on Flowergate. Xbox, bit of food, bed about midnight. I didn't go out again. I didn't speak to Uncle Graham after the pub. I've got a missed call from him on my phone at 01:18 and I didn't see it till the morning.

We argued about money, yeah. He's got money and he'd rather put it in a glass case. That's not a reason to hurt anybody.
items.note: Officer's note: on 29 Oct R. Lythe was arrested on suspicion of theft (Saltwick Bay). He answered "no comment" to all questions except one; see his phone download.

items.title: Neil Featherstone
items.name: Neil Featherstone
items.text:
Graham was my friend for twenty years. Yes, we disagreed about the ichthyosaur. I thought he was mad to give away something like that. That was his business.

I was home all night in Ruswarp. I got in about quarter past nine. Lorraine went up about midnight. I don't sleep well, I never have, and I was up and down, out the front with a roll-up. You can check the doorbell, it'll show I never left.

I've got a missed call from Graham at 01:17. My phone was face down on silent and I didn't see it till morning. I'll regret that for the rest of my life.

Saltwick? I don't know anything about Saltwick.

items.title: Lorraine Featherstone
items.name: Lorraine Featherstone
items.text:
Neil smokes, and I won't have it in the house, so he does it on the front step in his dressing gown. He can't settle when there's a deal on. He said he was waiting to hear about some stock coming in. I went up about quarter past twelve and heard him go in and out a few times. The van never moved, I'd have heard it. It's right under our window.

It's just the two of us in the house. My bike's in the shed out the back; Neil's never been on it in his life, before you ask, he's not the type.

items.title: Shaun Hebden
items.name: Shaun Hebden
items.text: Mary Ellen's not been out since Thursday. Saturday night I was in on Esk Terrace with the telly and a few cans. I know Ryan, everyone knows Ryan. I don't know nothing about any fossil.
items.note: Officer's note: arrested 29 Oct on suspicion of theft. No comment.

items.title: Carol Lythe
items.name: Carol Lythe
items.text:
Graham was Keith's brother. Since Keith passed in 2021 Graham's been good to us, mostly. I went round Thursday. We had words about money, I'm not ashamed of that, things have been tight since Keith. He said no.

Saturday I was home all day, did some baking, went to bed about half eleven. I couldn't sleep. I rang our Emma, she's in Canada, British Columbia, eight hours behind us. I rang her from bed about one o'clock and we talked until two, then I must have dropped off. I knew nothing till Ryan rang me Sunday dinnertime. Ryan had said he had a bit of work on that weekend, that's all I know.

Graham and his fossils. Honestly, if anybody had told him there were folk down at Saltwick messing with that fossil of his, he'd have been up those steps in his slippers, middle of the night or not. That was Graham.

items.title: Emma Stroud
items.subject: Statement: my call with Mum
items.text:
To whom it may concern,

I'm Carol Lythe's daughter. I'm told you need to know about my call with Mum on the Saturday.

I finished a day shift and got home about quarter to six. Mum video-called me on WhatsApp at about two minutes past six. I know because I'd just put the oven on for the kids' tea. We talked until nearly seven, when I had to go because we had a table booked at a quarter past.

It was a bad line at her end, really windy, I kept losing her. She said she couldn't sleep and had the window open. She was chatty, a bit wired, kept asking about the kids.

I can't believe Uncle Graham is gone.

Emma Stroud, RN (ICU)
Golden, British Columbia
+1 (250) 555-0143

items.title: Theft report, Saltwick Bay
body: The landowner's agent reports the removal of a large block from the cliff foot at Saltwick Bay. There are fresh tool marks, and a strop buckle was left on the scar. Mr G. Lythe had shown the agent the block on 4 October, and recovery by a museum team was booked for 2 November. The block has not been recovered.
